questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms is the most efficient in the average case for large datasets?
a. Bubble Sort
b. Quick Sort
c. Selection Sort
d. Insertion Sort
questions.explanation: Quick sort runs in O(n log n) on average with small constant factors and good cache locality, so it is usually fastest in practice on large arrays, although its worst case is O(n²).

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Radix Sort?
a. O(nk)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n log n)
d. O(n³)
questions.explanation: Radix sort performs one counting pass per digit position, so the cost is O(nk) for k digits. It is not a comparison-based sort, which is why it can beat O(n log n).

questions.question:
What is the worst-case time complexity of the Quick Sort algorithm?
a. O(n log n)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n)
d. O(log n)
questions.explanation: Quick sort degrades to O(n²) when the pivot is always the smallest or largest element, for example a sorted array with a first-element pivot. A random pivot avoids that in practice.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct time complexity for constructing a Max-Heap?
a. O(n log n)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n)
d. O(log n)
questions.explanation: Building a max-heap bottom-up, starting from the last internal node and sifting down, costs O(n) because most nodes are near the leaves. Inserting elements one by one would cost O(n log n).

questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
a) Bubble sort
b) Merge sort
c) Selection sort
d) Insertion sort
questions.explanation: Merge sort splits and merges identically whatever the input order, so it stays O(n log n) in the best, average and worst cases. Bubble, selection and insertion sort reach O(n²).

questions.question:
The given array is arr = {1, 2, 4, 3}. Bubble sort is used to sort the array elements. How many iterations will be done to sort the array?
a) 4
b) 2
c) 1
d) 0
questions.explanation: Only the pair 4, 3 is out of order, so the first pass swaps them and the second pass finds no swaps and stops. Two passes therefore sort this nearly ordered array.

questions.question:
Choose the incorrect statement about merge sort from the following:
a) it is a comparison based sort
b) it is an adaptive algorithm
c) it is not an in-place algorithm
d) it is a stable algorithm

options.A: it is a comparison based sort
options.C: it is not an in-place algorithm

questions.explanation: Merge sort does the same work whatever the input order, so it is not adaptive; its O(n log n) never improves on sorted data. It is comparison based, stable and not in place.

questions.question:
What is a randomized QuickSort?
a) The leftmost element is chosen as the pivot
b) The rightmost element is chosen as the pivot
c) Any element in the array is chosen as the pivot
d) A random number is generated which is used as the pivot

options.A: The leftmost element is chosen as the pivot
options.B: The rightmost element is chosen as the pivot
options.C: Any element in the array is chosen as the pivot
options.D: A random number is generated which is used as the pivot

questions.explanation: Randomized quick sort picks the pivot uniformly at random, which makes the O(n²) case very unlikely whatever the input order. A fixed end-element pivot does not have that guarantee.

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithm implementations is similar to that of an insertion sort?
a) Binary heap
b) Quick sort
c) Merge sort
d) Radix sort
questions.explanation: Heap sort builds a heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum into a growing sorted region, which resembles inserting items into a sorted part one at a time. Its structure is nearest to insertion sort.

questions.question:
What is the maximum number of swaps that can be performed in the Selection Sort algorithm?
a) n-1
b) n
c) 1
d) n-2
questions.explanation: Selection sort swaps once per pass and there are n-1 passes, so at most n-1 swaps are made. That low swap count is its main advantage over bubble sort.

questions.question:
If the array is already sorted, which of these algorithms will exhibit the best performance?
a) Merge Sort
b) Insertion Sort
c) Quick Sort
d) Heap Sort
questions.explanation: Insertion sort scans an already sorted array once, shifting nothing, so its best case is O(n). Quick and heap sort still do O(n log n) work.

questions.question:
What is the maximum number of swaps that can be performed in the Bubble Sort algorithm?
a) n-1
b) n
c) 1
d) n*(n-1)/2
questions.explanation: In the worst case, a reverse-sorted array, bubble sort swaps once for every pair of positions, giving n(n-1)/2 swaps. That equals the number of inversions in the array.

questions.question:
Quick Sort algorithm is a:
a) Dynamic Programming
b) Computer programming
c) Divide & Conquer Algorithm
d) Greedy algorithm
questions.explanation: Quick sort partitions around a pivot and recurses on the two parts, which is divide and conquer. Dynamic programming and greedy methods are different strategies.

questions.question:
Running time complexity of heap sort is ________.
a) O(n)
b) O(n²)
c) O(n log n)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: Heap sort builds the heap in O(n) and performs n extractions at O(log n) each, giving O(n log n) in every case with only O(1) extra space.

questions.question:
Time complexity of insertion sort is ________.
a) O(n)
b) O(n log n)
c) O(n²)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: Insertion sort compares and shifts elements for every new item, so a reverse-sorted array costs about n²/2 operations: O(n²) worst case and O(n) when already sorted.

questions.question:
What is pivot in Quick Sort?
a) The first element of the array
b) The last element of the array
c) A reference element used to partition the array
d) The median element of the array

options.A: The first element of the array
options.B: The last element of the array
options.C: A reference element used to partition the array
options.D: The median element of the array

questions.explanation: The pivot is the reference value used to partition the array: smaller elements go left and larger ones right. It need not be the first, last or median element.

questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms is the fastest?
a) Merge sort
b) Quick sort
c) Insertion sort
d) Shell sort
questions.explanation: Quick sort is usually fastest in practice because of low overhead and sequential memory access, even though merge sort has the better worst-case bound.

a) Merge Sort

questions.explanation: Shell sort generalises insertion sort by first sorting elements a gap apart, which reduces the shifting needed later. The gap shrinks until it reaches 1.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Count Sort where n is the number of elements and k is the range of input?
a) O(n log n)
b) O(n + k)
c) O(nk)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Counting sort builds a frequency array of size k and scans the n items, so the time is O(n + k). It works only for integer keys in a known range.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true about Heap Sort?
a) It is not an in-place sorting algorithm
b) It has O(n²) worst-case time complexity
c) It is an in-place sorting algorithm with O(n log n) complexity
d) It requires O(n) extra space

options.A: It is not an in-place sorting algorithm
options.B: It has O(n²) worst-case time complexity
options.C: It is an in-place sorting algorithm with O(n log n) complexity

questions.explanation: Heap sort rearranges the array itself, needing only O(1) auxiliary space, and guarantees O(n log n) in all cases. Merge sort, by contrast, needs O(n) extra space.

What is the space complexity of Merge Sort?
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n log n)
questions.explanation: Merging needs a temporary buffer holding up to n elements, so merge sort uses O(n) auxiliary space. The recursion stack adds only O(log n).

questions.question:
What is the best-case time complexity of Bubble Sort (with optimization)?
a) O(n²)
b) O(n log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(1)
questions.explanation: Optimised bubble sort stops as soon as a pass makes no swaps, so a sorted array finishes after one pass: O(n). Without that flag it stays O(n²).

Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT stable?
a) Merge Sort
b) Insertion Sort
c) Heap Sort
d) Bubble Sort
questions.explanation: Heap sort is not stable, because sifting elements around the heap can reverse the relative order of equal keys. Merge, insertion and bubble sort are stable.
